chunks: "It depends on which kind of termination, but the rule is: series termination at the source, as close to the driver pin as possible, and parallel termination at the end of the line, at or just past the last receiver.
Not in the middle. Series termination works by making the driver's output impedance plus the resistor equal Z0.
The driver launches half the voltage, the full voltage appears at the far end, and the reflection that returns is absorbed by the matched source.

For that to work, the resistor has to sit right at the driver, because the bit of trace between the driver pin and the resistor is a stub that sees the unmatched driver, so I keep it to a few millimetres.

Parallel termination absorbs the wave when it arrives, so it has to be at the far end, beyond the receiver, because anything beyond the terminator isn't terminated; and the connection from the line to the resistor needs to be short, so the receiver pin and resistor are effectively at the same point.
In the middle, a series resistor just splits the line into two mismatched pieces and a parallel resistor loads it.
So the line passes through the receiver pad and ends at the resistor, with a short via to the plane or to the termination rail."
